name: io.github.oculonlive/oculon
title: Oculon
description: OSINT checks with sources: scams, links, claims, recalls, travel risk, CVEs, outages, research.

tools.name: oculon_radar
tools.description: Global anomaly radar. Finds what the world is suddenly paying attention to right now (Wikipedia readership spikes, Hacker News traction, Polymarket swings, strong earthquakes, severe natural events) and fuses items about the same subject into corroborated signals with evidence.

tools.name: oculon_scoreboard

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_url_check
tools.description: Is a link dangerous? Checks Google Safe Browsing, URLhaus (abuse.ch), urlscan.io scan history, domain age and registrar (RDAP), and warning signs in the URL itself (brand names on other domains, punycode, risky TLDs). Returns a verdict (malicious, suspicious, no known threats), a 0-100 risk and the reasons.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_audit
tools.description: Dependency audit for developers. Pass the text of a package.json or requirements.txt, or items like "npm:express@4.17.1 pypi:requests==2.19.0". For each package: known vulnerabilities with CVSS, deprecation, last release, versions behind, OpenSSF Scorecard and maintenance, license; plus a 0-100 risk. Source: deps.dev.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_fact_check
tools.description: Fact check a claim, or the main claim of a news link. Finds published fact checks (Google Fact Check Tools: Snopes, AFP, PolitiFact, Full Fact and others) and current reporting, then gives a verdict (true, mostly true, mixed, misleading, false, unverified) with a confidence and a summary that cites the numbered sources.

claim.description: The claim, or a URL of an article

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_travel
tools.description: Travel and place risk brief for the coming week: US State Department and UK FCDO advice, 7-day weather warnings (storms, heavy rain, gusts, heat, cold, UV), PM2.5 air quality, WHO disease outbreak news, GDACS disaster alerts, nearby earthquakes, satellite heat detections and confirmed internet outages. Returns a level (low, moderate, high, severe) with the reasons.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_scam_check
tools.description: Is this message a scam? Paste an SMS, email or chat message. Every link is checked (Safe Browsing, URLhaus, urlscan.io, domain age, look-alikes), the sender domain is compared with any brand it mentions, and known scam patterns are matched (parcel fees, account locked, one-time codes, gift cards or crypto, "hi mum" new number, prizes, job and investment promises). Returns likely scam, suspicious or no strong signs, a 0-100 risk, the reasons and what to do.

message.description: The full text of the message, including the sender line if there is one

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_recall
tools.description: Is this car or product recalled? Pass a 17-character VIN, "year make model" (e.g. "2018 Honda Accord"), or a product name ("stroller", "peanut butter"). Vehicles: NHTSA safety recalls with do-not-drive and park-outside warnings. Products: CPSC consumer recalls and FDA food, drug and device enforcement reports.

query.description: VIN, "year make model", or product name

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_email_security
tools.description: Can someone send email that looks like it comes from this domain? Checks SPF, DMARC, DKIM, MTA-STS, TLS reporting, BIMI, CAA and DNSSEC from public DNS, and returns a verdict (spoofable, partly protected, protected), a 0-100 score and the fixes in order.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_ip_check
tools.description: Who runs this IP address, and is it known for abuse? Pass an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a domain (its first address is checked). Returns network (ASN, owner, type), location, flags (Tor exit, proxy, hosting, internet scanner, known benign service), AbuseIPDB reports, GreyNoise scanner status, AlienVault OTX threat reports, VirusTotal engine verdicts, ThreatFox malware infrastructure, Spamhaus DROP listing and open ports, with a verdict (malicious, suspicious, no known abuse), a 0-100 risk and the reasons.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_hash_check
tools.description: Is this file known malware, a known good file, or unknown? Pass an MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash. Checks CIRCL hashlookup (NIST NSRL and other known-software sets), MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox, AlienVault OTX and VirusTotal, and returns a verdict, the malware family when known, the reasons and what to do.

hash.description: MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 in hex

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_ransomware
tools.description: Ransomware leak-site claims collected by ransomware.live. Leave query empty for the newest claims, or pass a two-letter country code ("DE"), a sector ("Healthcare", "Manufacturing") or a company name or domain. Returns victims with group, country, sector and dates, plus counts by group, country and sector. These are claims by criminals and can be wrong.

query.description: Optional: country code, sector, company or domain

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_company_lookup
tools.description: Is this company or supplier real? Pass an EU VAT number (checked live in the European Commission VIES service: valid or not, registered name and address), a 20-character LEI, or a company name (Global LEI Index: legal name, registered address, status, registration number, ultimate parent). Useful before paying an invoice from a new supplier.

query.description: Company name, LEI, or EU VAT number such as "NL004495445B01"

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_breaches
tools.description: Data breaches from Have I Been Pwned: leave domain empty for the newest breaches, or pass a domain or company name for all of its breaches, with date, accounts affected and the kinds of data exposed.

domain.description: Optional: domain or company name, e.g. "adobe.com"

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_phone_check
tools.description: Who is behind this phone number? Pass it in international format (+44 20 7946 0958), or a national number with country. Returns country, line type (mobile, landline, VoIP, premium rate), carrier and location when known, and warnings for premium-rate numbers, UK 070 personal numbers and the Caribbean "one ring" callback-scam area codes. Never looks up the owner.

country.description: ISO country code for a national number, e.g. "US"

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_iban_check
tools.description: Check an IBAN before paying an invoice, fully offline: country, length, ISO 13616 mod-97 check digits and the bank code. Pass the supplier country to flag an account held in another country, a common sign of invoice fraud. A valid IBAN does not prove who owns the account.

country.description: Optional: the supplier's ISO country code, e.g. "NL"

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_email_headers
tools.description: Analyze the raw headers of a suspicious email: SPF, DKIM and DMARC results recorded by the receiving server, the Received path, the origin IP and its country, and spoofing signs (From differs from the envelope sender, Reply-To elsewhere, a display name posing as an address). Returns a verdict and risk.

headers.description: The raw message headers, as shown by "Show original"

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_lookalike_domains
tools.description: Find lookalike domains of a brand that a phisher could use: typos, swapped letters, homoglyphs, extra words and other endings that exist in DNS (with mail servers), plus certificates issued in the last 90 days for any name containing the brand (Certificate Transparency).

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_honeypot_check
tools.description: Can this token be sold? Simulates a buy and a sell on the token's main pool and replays recent holders' sells (honeypot.is): honeypot verdict, buy and sell tax, holders who could not sell, unpublished or upgradeable contracts. Chains: eth, bsc, base.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_address_check
tools.description: Check a crypto address before sending funds, without API keys: chain from the address format (Bitcoin, EVM, Solana, Tron), US OFAC sanctions, and balance, transaction count and labels from free explorers (mempool.space, Blockscout, Solana RPC). Flags unused addresses and contracts posing as wallets.

network.description: Optional for 0x addresses: "robinhood" for Robinhood Chain, default Ethereum

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_doc_check
tools.description: Was this invoice, bank statement or payment screenshot edited? Reads a PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JPEG or PNG: macros, remote templates, DDE fields, embedded objects and hidden sheets in Office files, the programs that made and saved it (online PDF editors, image editors), creation vs modification date, how many times it was saved, fonts embedded twice, white boxes over text, annotations, dangerous parts (JavaScript, launch actions), and checks every IBAN in its text. Screenshots are read with a free AI vision model when a key is set. A clean result is not proof the document is genuine.

url.description: Or an https URL of the file

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_approvals
tools.description: Who can take tokens out of this wallet right now: every ERC-20 and NFT approval the wallet signed (Etherscan logs), re-read on chain so revoked ones drop out. Spenders are named (Uniswap, 1inch, OpenSea...) or flagged: plain wallets, unverified contracts and unknown contracts with unlimited access. Spam approval events from fake tokens are filtered. Gives a revoke.cash link. Chains: eth, arbitrum, polygon.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_contract_risk
tools.description: What the owner of a token contract can still do to holders: mint, blacklist, pause trading, change taxes, limit wallets, change balances, upgrade the code (proxy), self-destruct. Read from verified source (Sourcify, Etherscan) or, for unverified contracts, from selectors in the bytecode. Plus current owner (renounced or not), proxy admin and implementation, holder concentration and locked liquidity (GoPlus), main pool and age (DexScreener). Chains: eth, base, bsc, arbitrum, polygon.

chain.description: eth, base, bsc, arbitrum or polygon (default eth)

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_signature_check
tools.description: Decode what a wallet signature request really allows before signing: EIP-712 typed data (ERC-2612 and DAI permits, Uniswap Permit2 allowances and transfers, Seaport orders that give NFTs away for nothing), transaction calldata or a {to, data, value} object (approve, setApprovalForAll, transfers, Permit2 approve, multicall bundles, unknown functions named via signature databases), and raw eth_sign hashes. Spenders are looked up on chain (wallet or contract, verified or not).

request.description: The request: typed data JSON, 0x calldata, a {to,data,value} JSON, or the message text

chain.description: Optional chain: eth, base, bsc, arbitrum, polygon

to.description: Optional: the contract the calldata is sent to (token address for approve)

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_address_poisoning
tools.description: Has someone planted lookalike addresses in this wallet's history? Finds addresses that share the first and last characters with ones the wallet really paid, zero-value transfers it never signed, and fake USDT/USDC tokens, and says whether funds were already sent to a lookalike. Chains: eth, arbitrum, polygon.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_trace_funds
tools.description: Follow where money went from an address (for example a scammer or a drained wallet): the largest outgoing flows priced in USD, hop by hop, until an exchange (where funds can be frozen), a mixer, a bridge, a contract or a sanctioned address. Labels from the open eth-labels dataset, transaction hashes for a report. Chains: eth, arbitrum, polygon.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_image_check
tools.description: Was this image made by AI, edited, or taken with a camera? Reads C2PA Content Credentials (generator app, actions, AI source type, organizations in the signing certificates), IPTC digital source type, generator settings and prompts left by Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI, NovelAI, InvokeAI and Midjourney, EXIF camera data and editing software. Read locally. Missing metadata proves nothing.

data.description: The image as base64 (JPEG, PNG or WebP, max 10 MB)

url.description: Or an https URL of the image

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_qr_check
tools.description: Read the QR code in a photo or screenshot (PNG or baseline JPEG, versions 1-15) and check where it leads: links go through the URL check (Safe Browsing, URLhaus, domain age, lookalikes, shorteners), crypto payment codes and addresses through the address check, SEPA payment codes get their IBAN checked, Wi-Fi, SMS and phone codes are explained. Catches fake parking, parcel and login QR codes (quishing).

url.description: Or an https URL of the image

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_repo_check
tools.description: Is this GitHub repository safe to clone and run? Built for fake job tests and "run our bot" scams: install hooks (npm preinstall/postinstall, setup.py, VS Code tasks that run on folder open), code that downloads and runs code, wallet extension and browser password theft, Discord/Telegram webhooks, obfuscation and code hidden past the edge of the screen, committed program files, owner account age and bought stars. Reads files through the GitHub API; nothing is run.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_domain_report
tools.description: One report for a domain, all parts run together: link check of the site, email protection (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), what it exposes to the internet (open ports, CVEs), lookalike domains, and the company behind the name. Each part keeps its verdict and sources; PDF report available through the check id.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_wallet_report
tools.description: One report for a wallet or token address. Wallet: address check (sanctions, activity), active approvals, address poisoning and where funds went. Token contract: contract risk, sell simulation and address check. PDF report available through the check id.

chain.description: eth, arbitrum, polygon, base or bsc (default eth)

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_site_check
tools.description: Open a web page and look for wallet drainers and phishing: wallet connection code next to permit, Permit2, setApprovalForAll or unlimited approve requests, a receiver address written into the script, token-balance APIs used to rank what to take, known drainer kits, seed phrase and login forms on the wrong domain, forms posting elsewhere, Telegram bot tokens and Discord webhooks in the code, lookalikes of known apps, plus the link check of the final address. Scripts are read, never run.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_tx_explain
tools.description: Explain a transaction in plain words: who called what, every token and NFT transfer, approvals given or removed, and the fee. Flags tokens taken from a wallet in a transaction it did not send (an earlier approval or permit being used), approvals to plain wallets or unverified contracts, and NFT collections handed over. Spam tokens faking transfers are recognized. Chains: eth, base, arbitrum, bsc, polygon (found automatically).

chain.description: Optional: eth, base, arbitrum, bsc, polygon

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_token_creator
tools.description: Who created this token and what is their record: the creator wallet and date, the other contracts it deployed, which of those tokens are dead today (no pool or under $1,000 of liquidity), its wallet age, and who first funded it (exchange or mixer, from eth-labels). Chains: eth, arbitrum, polygon.

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_email_file
tools.description: Check a whole email file (.eml): SPF, DKIM, DMARC and spoofing in the headers, the message and every link through the scam check, and each attachment through the document check (PDF, Office), the QR reader and image check (images), or the malware hash lookup. Flags risky attachment types (programs, scripts, HTML, disk images).

tools.name: oculon_apk_check
tools.description: Is this Android app (APK) safe to install? Reads its manifest: package, version, every permission, and the ones banking trojans use (reading SMS codes, accessibility services, drawing over other apps, notification access, device admin, installing other apps); the signing certificate (debug keys flagged); and the SHA-256 in malware databases. Nothing is installed or run.

url.description: Or an https URL of the APK

tools.name: oculon_job_check
tools.description: Is this job offer a scam? tools.name: oculon_photo_location
tools.description: Where and when was this photo taken? GPS position and capture time from its EXIF data, the place name (OpenStreetMap), and the weather and daylight at that place and hour (Open-Meteo, sun position), so claims about a photo can be checked. Flags capture and GPS times that disagree. EXIF can be edited.

tools.name: oculon_invite_check
tools.description: What is behind a Telegram (t.me) or Discord (discord.gg) invite before joining: name, members and online, verified badge, Telegram scam or fake labels, server creation date, and the fake support or fake project pattern (brand plus "official", "support", "airdrop" without a verified badge).

brief.description: Short answer for agents: verdict, risk, top reasons, sources and check id (fewer tokens)

tools.name: oculon_stock_token

A ticker (TSLA) gives the official contract, ISIN, which sessions trade, the live bid and ask per token (adjusted by the corporate-action multiplier), daily range, volume, supply on chain, and upcoming dividends and splits. An address says whether it is an official Stock Token, and flags tokens that copy a ticker or call themselves Robinhood tokens without being on the list. tools.name: oculon_papers
tools.description: Research brief on a topic: the most cited papers of recent years, the newest relevant ones, papers per year (is the field growing?), PubMed counts for medical topics, and a short overview that cites the numbered papers. Sources: OpenAlex, PubMed, Semantic Scholar.
